relations.myth: Temple vow after victory over the Sallentini
relations.note: Regulus allegedly vowed or dedicated a temple to Pales after victory.

relations.myth: Regulus keeps his oath to Carthage
relations.note: Jupiter implicitly guarantees the enemy oath that compels Regulus to return.
They allegedly permit Carthaginian cruelty so Regulus earns greater glory.
Fortune overturns Regulus's success after his arrogant peace demands.
Seneca portrays Regulus as morally victorious over Fortune through steadfast suffering.

relations.myth: Horatian juxtaposition of Augustus and Regulus
relations.note: Horace juxtaposes Augustus's prospective divinity and eastern policy with Regulus's example.

relations.myth: Herculean framing of the Bagradas serpent
relations.note: Silius models Regulus's serpent exploit on Herculean monster combats without identifying them.
The African serpent is compared to the Hydra as a literary monster type.
Horace contrasts captive Romans' forgetfulness of Vesta with Regulus's fidelity.
Regulus and his army battle an enormous serpent using artillery.
Regulus's army kills the serpent with siege engines and sends its remains to Rome.
